findings.claim: Across the full observed window the landmark_00 soft-mass coordinate shows no net whole-window displacement (whole_window_z near zero) despite large opposing first-node and last-node rate z-scores, so the endpoint cloud is not drifting monotonically in this coordinate.

Landmark_00 local shape coordinates (cxx, cyy, czz, cyz, cxy, dx, dy, dz) all show multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts with no accepted polynomial, indicating oscillatory rather than staged monotone coordinate change over the window.

The learning window and observed score nodes span 0.0 to 0.5 with 50 evenly spaced score clocks, and the objective is final predicted target affinity primary with coordinate control only, so any coordinate reward must be evaluated against endpoint affinity rather than treated as the objective itself.

hypotheses.direction: test registered temporal_recipe levels at fixed dose_factors=1; do not reverse the affinity objective
hypotheses.falsifier: if the compiled schedule produces no change in realized per-node coordinate traces, or if endpoint affinity does not improve relative to the constant-curvature control, the stage-dependent hypothesis is not supported
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_00_local_cxx/cyy rate z-scores across observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: A stage-dependent curvature schedule (registered C1/C2/C3 recipes) may be worth testing at fixed dose because landmark_00 coordinate rates change sign within the window, so a single constant curvature may not match the observed early-versus-late contrast.

hypotheses.direction: retain constant curvature unless a registered time-varying recipe shows a reproducible trace change
hypotheses.falsifier: if C2 and a time-varying recipe yield indistinguishable coordinate traces, the time-varying edit is not justified
hypotheses.observable: whole-window z and sign-change counts for landmark_00 features
hypotheses.statement: Because landmark_00 soft mass shows no net whole-window trend while local shape coordinates oscillate, a constant-curvature control (C2) is a reasonable baseline against which any time-varying curvature must demonstrate a measurable trace difference.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; only continuous curves and trend tables were read.
No decoded final affinity labels are present in role input, so selection preference and coordinate trends cannot be equated with measured final benefit.
Coordinate features are untyped predicted-endpoint world-coordinate proxies; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is made.
The observed curves were not individually read via get_curve in this turn; findings rest on the continuous_trends table rows and clock metadata.
